name: Ouroboros Energy ThermalSink UR-3 District Waste Heat Exchange Network
product_name: Ouroboros Energy ThermalSink UR-3 District Waste Heat Exchange Network
description:
The ThermalSink UR-3 is a district-scale thermal infrastructure system that captures waste heat from industrial processes, server farms, transit systems, and dense commercial blocks across a defined urban grid sector and redistributes it as usable thermal energy through a network of insulated glycol-water carrier pipes and heat exchanger nodes. Each node — roughly the size of a utility cabinet — manages bidirectional thermal flow, accepting excess heat from high-output sources and delivering it to residential and commercial buildings for space heating, hot water, and agricultural thermal regulation. The UR-3 improves on earlier district heating models by using Ouroboros's proprietary dynamic routing algorithm, which continuously rebalances thermal loads across the network in response to real-time demand and source availability, reducing peak waste heat venting by up to 67%.

The system is physically anchored to Meridian 88's existing utility conduit infrastructure via Palladian Construction-licensed penetration sleeves, meaning installation requires negotiation with both Ouroboros and Palladian for rights-of-way in newer districts. In legacy zones the pipes often run exposed along building exteriors, wrapped in spray-on aerogel insulation that degrades visibly over years without maintenance. Ouroboros operates the UR-3 networks on a metered access model — buildings tap in through licensed exchange units and are billed per gigajoule of thermal energy consumed, with tiered pricing that penalizes draws during peak industrial input cycles.

The ThermalSink UR-3 has become the backbone of winter habitability in several mid-tier residential districts where building heating systems were never modernized. Ouroboros uses its control of the network's routing algorithm as leverage in municipal contract negotiations — documented incidents of 'thermal rebalancing events' that coincidentally dropped output to districts in payment dispute with the corponation have been reported but never successfully prosecuted. Informal tap-ins using homemade heat exchanger rigs are common in the lower districts and are technically prosecutable as energy theft under Meridian 88's Utility Asset statutes.
enables: agricultural thermal stabilization for urban grow systems
thermal mapping of urban industrial activity
social_impact: Ouroboros Energy's control of the ThermalSink UR-3 network has translated directly into political leverage — the corponation effectively holds veto power over winter habitability in any district connected to its grid. This has made Ouroboros a de facto governance actor in zoning decisions, construction approvals, and labor dispute mediations, since the implicit threat of a 'routing recalibration' during a cold snap carries more weight than most contractual enforcement mechanisms. Residents who have built their survival infrastructure around the network have no realistic exit option, as alternative heating systems would require capital investment far beyond lower-tier means.
story_hooks: A routing anomaly in the UR-3 network has been quietly diverting excess thermal capacity to an unmapped subterranean location for eleven months — Ouroboros's own engineers either don't know or aren't saying
A whistleblower inside Ouroboros has logs showing deliberate thermal restriction events disguised as algorithmic rebalancing, timed precisely to labor organizing meetings in affected districts

An independent engineer has designed a community-scale thermal buffer tank that could insulate a block from UR-3 supply interruptions — Ouroboros is moving to acquire her workshop through a subsidiary
The ThermalSink network's carrier pipes run directly beneath a district where Dredge Mining Collective has begun exploratory drilling — the vibration is causing microfractures in the pipe joints
